source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 8: book page 295. The book prints no answers for Unit 11.

blocks.prompt: 8 (a) A robotic arm moves such that: its \(x\)-position increases linearly at 2 m/s, its \(y\)-position follows \(y(t) = t^{2}\), its \(z\)-position is given by \(z(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\). Construct the position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do components formula ki shakal mein diye hain, lekin \(x\) wala component lafzon mein bayan hua hai.
Diya kya hai? \(x\) har second 2 m barhta hai, \(y(t) = t^{2}\), \(z(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\).
Find kya karna hai? Pehle \(x(t)\), phir poora \(\mathbf{r}(t)\).
Plan: 'linearly at 2 m/s' ka matlab \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\); shuru mein \(x = 0\) maan kar \(x = 2t\) likho, phir teenon jor do.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2\), \(y(t) = t^{2}\), \(z(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\).
Tareeqa: \(x(t)\) nikal kar teenon components jorenge (11.1.3 ke Step-1 se Step-3).

\(x\) wala component
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2 \ \Rightarrow \ x(t) = 2t\]
Kyun: jo cheez ek jaisi raftaar (2 m/s) se barhti hai woh har second 2 m barhti hai, yani \(t\) seconds mein \(2t\). Kitab shuru ki jagah nahin batati, is liye hum \(x(0) = 0\) maan lete hain.
Dhyan dein: 'linearly at 2 m/s' ko \(x = 2\) likh dena ghalat hai; 2 raftaar hai, position nahin.

Position vector
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = 2t\,\hat{i} + t^{2}\hat{j} + (1 - e^{-t})\hat{k}\]
Kyun: har component apne unit vector ke saath: \(x\) ke saath \(\hat{i}\), \(y\) ke saath \(\hat{j}\), \(z\) ke saath \(\hat{k}\).

Tasdeeq
Agar arm \(x = x_{0}\) se shuru ho to \(x(t) = x_{0} + 2t\). Lekin constant \(x_{0}\) differentiate karne par zero ho jata hai, is liye parts (b) aur (c) ke jawab nahin badlenge. Is liye hamara maanna jawab ko kharab nahin karta.
blocks.final_answer: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 2t\,\hat{i} + t^{2}\hat{j} + (1 - e^{-t})\hat{k}\) metres (\(t = 0\) par \(x = 0\) maan kar).

blocks.prompt: 8 (b) A robotic arm moves such that: its \(x\)-position increases linearly at 2 m/s, its \(y\)-position follows \(y(t) = t^{2}\), its \(z\)-position is given by \(z(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\). Find the velocity vector at \(t = 1\) sec.
blocks.explanation:
Velocity position ka derivative hai; position humein part (a) mein mil gayi.
Diya kya hai? \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 2t\,\hat{i} + t^{2}\hat{j} + (1 - e^{-t})\hat{k}\).
Find kya karna hai? \(t = 1\) second par velocity vector.
Plan: har component ko differentiate karo (\(e^{-t}\) par chain rule ka minus yaad rakho), phir \(t = 1\) rakho.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 2t\,\hat{i} + t^{2}\hat{j} + (1 - e^{-t})\hat{k}\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{v}(1)\).
Tareeqa: \(\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{r}'(t)\), har component alag.

Velocity
\[\mathbf{v}(t) = 2\,\hat{i} + 2t\,\hat{j} + e^{-t}\hat{k}\]
Kyun: \(2t \to 2\), \(t^{2} \to 2t\). Teesre component mein 1 ka derivative zero, aur \(e^{-t}\) ka derivative chain rule se \(-e^{-t}\); to \(-(-e^{-t}) = +e^{-t}\).
Dhyan dein: do minus mil kar plus bante hain; yahan sign ki ghalti aam hai.

Matlab
\[|\mathbf{v}(1)| = \sqrt{4 + 4 + e^{-2}} \approx 2.85 \text{ m/s}\]
Arm taqreeban 2.85 m/s se chal raha hai, zyada tar \(x\) aur \(y\) ki simt mein, aur upar bohat aahista uth raha hai.

blocks.prompt: 8 (c) A robotic arm moves such that: its \(x\)-position increases linearly at 2 m/s, its \(y\)-position follows \(y(t) = t^{2}\), its \(z\)-position is given by \(z(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\). Compute the acceleration at \(t = 1\) sec.
blocks.explanation:
Acceleration velocity ka derivative hai; velocity part (b) mein mil chuki hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\mathbf{v}(t) = 2\,\hat{i} + 2t\,\hat{j} + e^{-t}\hat{k}\).
Find kya karna hai? \(t = 1\) second par acceleration.
Plan: \(\mathbf{v}(t)\) ko ek dafa aur differentiate karo, \(t = 1\) rakho, aur har component ka matlab samjho.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{v}(t) = 2\,\hat{i} + 2t\,\hat{j} + e^{-t}\hat{k}\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{a}(1)\).
Tareeqa: \(\mathbf{a}(t) = \mathbf{v}'(t)\).

Acceleration
\[\mathbf{a}(t) = 0\,\hat{i} + 2\,\hat{j} - e^{-t}\hat{k}\]
\[\mathbf{a}(1) = 2\,\hat{j} - e^{-1}\hat{k}\]
\[\approx 2\,\hat{j} - 0.368\,\hat{k}\]
Kyun: constant 2 ka derivative zero; \(2t\) ka 2; aur \(e^{-t}\) ka \(-e^{-t}\) (chain rule ka minus).
Dhyan dein: \(\mathbf{v}(1)\) ko differentiate mat kijiye, woh to ek fixed vector hai; \(\mathbf{v}(t)\) ko kijiye.

Matlab
\(x\)-direction mein koi acceleration nahin, yani \(x\) ki raftaar hamesha 2 m/s rehti hai. \(y\) ki raftaar har second 2 m/s barhti hai. \(z\) ki raftaar ghat rahi hai (minus sign), yani arm ki oonchai aahista aahista \(z = 1\) m ki taraf ruk rahi hai, kyunke \(e^{-t}\) waqt ke saath zero ki taraf jata hai. Jaise lift apni manzil ke qareeb aa kar dheemi ho jati hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.3 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (Unit 11 ki kisi exercise ke jawab kitab mein nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) jaise angles radians mein hain, is liye calculator RAD mode mein rakhein. Apna hal yahan wale hal se mila kar dekhiye.
